findings.title: Reschedule still uses immediate SendGrid cancellation
findings.body: The newly added reschedule path calls `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)`, passing `immediateDelete=true`. The PR description and design (move cancellation to the CRON to avoid SendGrid's 100 pending cancellations limit) only makes sense with the deferred approach. Calling SendGrid synchronously here reintroduces the exact bug being fixed: a reschedule flurry can hit the 100-pending-cancellations cap, leaving previously scheduled email reminders un-cancelled. Should be `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId)` (no third arg) to mark `cancelled=true` and let the CRON do the SendGrid call, matching the approach used in `handleCancelBooking.ts` and elsewhere.

findings.title: Use of private Prisma client type
findings.body: `const workflowRemindersToDelete: Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[] = [];` references a private/internal Prisma generated type (`Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient`). Such types are not part of Prisma's public API and are subject to change between Prisma versions, which can silently break compilation. Use a public type such as `Prisma.PrismaPromise<WorkflowReminder>` or simply `Promise<WorkflowReminder>`.

findings.title: Cancellation query missing method filter
findings.body: The new cancellation query only filters by `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, with no `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` filter. The same `workflowReminder` table also holds SMS reminders, and although the current SMS code hard-deletes rows, a future code path that sets `cancelled=true` on SMS rows (or a manual DB edit) would cause this CRON to attempt to POST `batch_id: null` to SendGrid's scheduled_sends endpoint and crash on null. Adding `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL` to the where clause makes the logic self-contained and consistent with the `deleteMany` block above it.

findings.title: immediateDelete=true leaves orphan DB rows
findings.body: When `immediateDelete` is true, the function calls SendGrid to cancel and `return`s without ever updating or deleting the `workflowReminder` row. The row therefore remains in the DB with `cancelled = null`, so the new CRON will not pick it up and there is no follow-up cleanup. The SMS path always hard-deletes its row regardless; the email path should at least mark `cancelled: true` (or delete) after the SendGrid call so the row is not orphaned, particularly since these callers (workflow delete, step delete, reschedule) may not cascade-delete the reminder row.

findings.title: Async functions in forEach are not awaited
findings.body: `originalRescheduledBooking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); })` invokes async functions without awaiting. The surrounding `try/catch` cannot capture rejections from these calls; any failure (e.g., SendGrid 4xx, Prisma error) becomes an unhandled rejection and the error handler `log.error("Error while canceling scheduled workflow reminders", error)` will never be executed. Use `await Promise.all(reminders.map(...))` inside the try/catch (or a `for/await`) so cancellations complete and errors are observable.

findings.title: Reminder cancellations fired from forEach without awaiting
findings.body: `updatedBookings.forEach((booking) => booking.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(...); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(...); }))` does not await the async reminder calls. The handler returns the success response while cancellations are still in flight. Errors from the internal `try/catch` of those helpers are merely logged via `console.log` and the caller never learns if a cancellation failed. Combined with the immediateDelete semantics, a failure means the cancelled booking can still trigger an outgoing workflow reminder. Convert to `await Promise.all(...)` or sequential `for/await`.

findings.title: Reschedule reminder cancellation not awaited
findings.body: In `requestReschedule`, `bookingToReschedule.workflowReminders.forEach((reminder) => { deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId); })` does not await the async deletion calls. Failures are only logged by the helpers' internal catch and never propagated to the caller, so a SendGrid/Prisma error leaves the reminder in place. With no surrounding try/catch, even logging of these errors disappears at this layer. Use `await Promise.all(...)`.

findings.title: Multiple reminder cancellation blocks fire-and-forget
findings.body: Several blocks in the `update` and `delete` mutations (`scheduledReminders.forEach`, `remindersToDelete.flat().forEach`, `remindersFromStep.forEach`, `remindersToUpdate.forEach`, `steps.forEach` calling `scheduleEmailReminder`/`scheduleSMSReminder`) iterate with `forEach` over async functions that are never awaited. Errors from SendGrid/Twilio/Prisma are swallowed inside the helpers' catch blocks. Use `await Promise.all(...)` (or sequential `for/await`) so failures are observable and cancellations actually complete before the workflow state changes.

findings.title: Cancellation loop is sequential
findings.body: Reminders are cancelled one at a time using `await client.request(...)` inside a `for (const reminder of remindersToCancel)` loop. With many reminders to cancel (the whole reason for deferring to a CRON), serializing SendGrid calls slows the CRON. The SendGrid cancel calls are independent, so they can run in parallel via `Promise.allSettled` to keep the request window short and reduce the chance that one slow call blocks the run. DB deletes can then be awaited in another `Promise.all`.

findings.title: Past-dated reminders deleted before cancellation runs
findings.body: The first block deletes every EMAIL reminder with `scheduledDate <= now()` regardless of `cancelled` or `scheduled` state, and the cancellation block runs after. A reminder that was just marked `cancelled=true` while its `scheduledDate` is still in the future (within ~1 hour) is fine, but the unconditional past-date delete means a reminder with `scheduled=false`, `cancelled=true`, and a `scheduledDate` that briefly slipped into the past (e.g., race during reschedule) will be silently deleted before the cancellation CRON ever tries to SendGrid-cancel it. Filter by `scheduled: true` (and/or `referenceId: { not: null }`) so unscheduled/cancelled reminders are not lost.

findings.title: New column is nullable with no default
findings.body: `ALTER TABLE "WorkflowReminder" ADD COLUMN "cancelled" BOOLEAN;` leaves the column nullable with no default. The CRON relies on `cancelled: true` (strict match) to pick up rows, so existing rows with `NULL` will never be processed. While intentional for new rows, any rows that were already scheduled in SendGrid for cancelled bookings prior to this migration will remain pending in SendGrid forever (the very bug this PR addresses). Either set a default of `false`, backfill, or add a one-off cleanup for legacy scheduled reminders.

findings.title: Workflow delete uses immediateDelete inconsistently
findings.body: In `delete` and the deleted-step branch of `update`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is used (`immediateDelete=true`). Other branches in the same file (e.g., `activeOn` change block at line 376 and edited-step block at line 569) call without `immediateDelete`. Deleting a workflow with many active bookings could therefore hit SendGrid's 100-pending-cancellations limit. Either drop `immediateDelete=true` everywhere for consistency with the PR's stated design, or document the choice explicitly.
